If you don't, you could have problems with your teeth and gums - like cavities or even tooth loss. Here's how to keep your mouth and teeth healthy: Brush your teeth twice a day with a fluoride toothpaste Clean between your teeth every day with floss or another type of between-the-teeth cleaner Snack smart - limit sugary snacks Don't smoke or chew tobacco See your dentist or oral health professional regularly NIH: National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research Start Here Oral Hygiene (National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research) Also in Spanish Taking Care of Your Teeth and Mouth (National Institute on Aging) Also in Spanish Diagnosis and Tests Dental Exam (National Library of Medicine) Also in Spanish Panoramic Dental X-Ray (American College of Radiology; Radiological Society of North America) Also in Spanish Treatments and Therapies Plaque: What It Is and How to Get Rid of It (National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research) - PDF Prevention of Infective Endocarditis Wallet Card (American Heart Association) - PDF Specifics Blood Thinners and Dental Care (American Academy of Oral Medicine) Taking on Teeth Grinding and Clenching: Halt Dental Damage and Jaw Pain (National Institutes of Health) Also in Spanish Statistics and Research FastStats: Oral and Dental Health (National Center for Health Statistics) Clinical Trials ClinicalTrials.gov: Dental Care (National Institutes of Health) ClinicalTrials.gov: Oral Health (National Institutes of Health) Journal Articles References and abstracts from MEDLINE/PubMed (National Library of Medicine) Article: Unravelling the benefits of thermal waters enhancing oral health: a pilot...
